I've got a walker, and I can't do stairs or a top bunk. Honestly, I can't walk far without stopping to rest.
Thank you for telling me. A walker, no stairs, and a rest stop on long walks. Got it. Do you have any ID with you right now, like a state ID or a birth certificate?
Nope, I lost my ID a while back. Everything I had went missing when I was living outside.
I'm sorry you lost your papers. Losing everything outside is hard. Which city were you living in before you came here?
Santa Ana, mostly. I had a spot near the river, under the bridge, until things got bad with my leg.
Santa Ana, and under the bridge by the river. Thank you. Last question for now: what kind of phone do you have, or do you not have one?
I've got a basic phone. It just does calls and texts, no internet or apps, so keep that in mind.
Got it, a basic phone with calls and texts only, no internet. I'll keep that in mind. Before we wrap up, have you ever served in the military?
Yeah, I did. Army, a long time ago. I don't really want to get into the details right now, though.

Thanks, that's enough for now, and we can skip the details. Here's what I heard: you're leaving Friday, you use a walker, you can't do stairs or a top bunk, and you rest on long walks. You don't have ID right now. You were living in Santa Ana, under the bridge by the river. You have a basic phone for calls and texts only. You served in the Army. Did I get that right?
Yeah, that's right. Friday, the walker, no stairs or top bunk, the rests, no ID, Santa Ana by the river, the basic phone, and the Army. You got it all.
Thank you. That's everything I need for now. I'll find your next step now, and your case manager will go over it with you.

transcript.text: Hi. I'm Sal, a helper on this tablet. I'm not a person, and a staff member will check everything with you. I'll ask a few short questions and take short notes for your case manager. You can skip any of them. What's on your mind most right now?
A guy told me there's a place that helps with deposits. Is that real?
I hear you. I can't say what help exists yet, but I'll write down that you're asking about deposits, so the next step can look into it. Are you planning to rent a place when you leave here?
Yeah, I'm hoping to get into a place once I get out. I've got some money saved up, but I don't know if it's enough for the deposit and first month.
Got it. You're hoping to rent a place, and you have some savings for the deposit and first month. Do you know roughly how much money you have saved?
Not exactly, maybe a few hundred bucks? I haven't sat down and added it up, to be honest.
A few hundred dollars. That's a good place to start, and we don't need the exact number. What city did you live in before you came here?
Um, I'd rather not say the city yet. I'm not sure this is the right place for me to be giving that out.
That's fair, you don't have to say. We can skip it. Do you have an ID card or any papers with your name on them right now?
Some of my papers got lost when I moved around, so I'm not sure what I still have. Why do you need to know that?
Fair question. It helps find a place to sleep and get a home, since some help needs an ID. You can skip it if you want. Have you served in the military?
Nah, never served. Why are you asking so much about me? I just wanted to know if this deposit thing is real.

Fair enough, you've been patient. Here's what I heard: you want to rent a place when you leave, you have a few hundred dollars saved for a deposit and first month, and some of your papers got lost. Did I get that right?
Yeah, that's right. I'm also still wondering if this program is actually running, though. Can you tell me what it's called?
Good, thanks for checking that with me. I can't name a program yet, and I won't guess. I'll find your next step now, and your case manager will go over the details with you.
